# Memory management

**Lab 2.** Allocate frames, map pages, grow the heap — then watch the boot log prove it.

## Layers

| Layer | Implementation | Location |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| **PMM** (physical) | Bitmap allocator, 4 KiB frames | `kernel/mm/pmm.zig` |
| **VMM** (virtual) | 4-level paging (PML4→PDPT→PD→PT) | `kernel/mm/vmm.zig` |
| **Kernel heap** | Linked-list / slab allocator | `kernel/mm/heap.zig` |
| **User heap** | `mmap`-style syscall | `sys_mem_map` (Phase 28) |

## PMM — bitmap over the Limine memory map

At boot, Limine hands over the physical memory map. The PMM marks usable frames free and reserves the kernel, then allocates with a bitmap (`kernel/mm/pmm.zig`, unit-tested on host):

```zig
// Conceptual shape (see kernel/mm/pmm.zig for the documented real code)
pub fn allocFrame() ?u64 {
    // Find the first clear bit, set it, return frame address.
}
pub fn freeFrame(frame: u64) void {
    // Clear the bit; the frame becomes reusable.
}
```

## VMM — four levels

`kernel/arch/x86_64/paging.zig` builds the page tables; `kernel/mm/vmm.zig` maps on demand (`mapPage`, `mapPageEnsure`). Page faults land in the IDT handler, which logs CR2 and the error code instead of silently dying.

## Per-process address spaces

Since Phase 25, each process owns a page table (`Process.page_table`, a CR3 value). The ELF loader maps a program only into its own table (`setTargetPml4` / `clearTargetPml4`), and ring-3 entry switches CR3 via the `R9 → CR3` convention in `usermode_jump.S`, restoring the kernel CR3 on return. Two processes can therefore load at the same virtual address without seeing each other — the boot test proves it:

```text
Page table per pid OK
Address space OK
```

## Lab 2 — memory markers

```bash
zig build run
# Expected serial lines (among others):
# PMM initialized, PMM alloc test OK, VMM initialized, Heap initialized
# Memory map test OK (100 frames), Heap test OK, Zinux boot OK
```

The full suite (`zig build boot-test`) additionally exercises `sys_mem_map`: create a memory capability, map one page into ring 3, write and read it back (`Mem map syscall OK`).
